mostWorthwhile.text: Building the decomposition loop was most worthwhile: fungi broke down wood, nutrients returned to soil, and roots used them for new growth. The sequence made the forest's interdependence tangible.

leastWorthwhile.text: Inspecting peat was a fairly predictable transition once burial was the remaining goal, although the automatic combination kept it brief.

surprise.text: The newly revealed cloud goal shifted my attention from soil to the atmosphere; the final combination explained how forests can contribute to rainfall beyond individual trees.

arbitrary.text: Combining fallen wood with partnered cells to make fungi initially felt like a leap, though the result clarified that the wood had not spontaneously become alive.

continue.text: Yes. I would be curious to see further connections between living systems and their surroundings; the nutrient loop and forest-rain link made this chapter engaging without presenting the myth as a literal recipe.
